content.prompt: Solve each equation by first dividing both sides by a common factor.

answer.worked:
Divide both sides by $2$.

$$\begin{align*}x^2+3x+2&=0\\(x+1)(x+2)&=0\\x+1&=0\quad\text{or}\quad x+2=0\\x&=-1\quad\text{or}\quad x=-2\end{align*}$$

Divide both sides by $3$.

$$\begin{align*}a^2-5a+6&=0\\(a-3)(a-2)&=0\\a-3&=0\quad\text{or}\quad a-2=0\\a&=3\quad\text{or}\quad a=2\end{align*}$$

Divide both sides by $4$.

$$\begin{align*}x^2+2x-35&=0\\(x+7)(x-5)&=0\\x+7&=0\quad\text{or}\quad x-5=0\\x&=-7\quad\text{or}\quad x=5\end{align*}$$

children.prompt: The rectangle is extended by $5$ cm to form a square. Form a quadratic equation and find $x$.

answer.worked:
The square has equal sides, so its length equals $x+5$ cm.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{50}{x}&=x+5\\50&=x(x+5)\\x^2+5x-50&=0\\(x+10)(x-5)&=0\\x&=-10\text{ or }x=5.\end{align*}$$
Reject $x=-10$ because a width must be positive. Hence $x=5\text{ cm}$. The original length is $50\div5=10$ cm, equal to the extended width $5+5=10$ cm.

A number is squared and then doubled. The result is 45 more than the original number. What is the original number?

answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the original number.

$$\begin{align*}2x^2&=x+45\\2x^2-x-45&=0\\(2x+9)(x-5)&=0\end{align*}$$

By the null factor law,

$$\begin{align*}2x+9&=0\quad\text{or}\quad x-5=0\\x&=-\frac{9}{2}\quad\text{or}\quad x=5.\end{align*}$$

Both satisfy the original statement: $2(5)^2=50=5+45$ and $2(-\frac{9}{2})^2=\frac{81}{2}=-\frac{9}{2}+45$.

The original number is $5$ or $-\frac{9}{2}$.

content.prompt: The difference of two numbers is 16 and the sum of their squares is 130. Find the two numbers.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the smaller number. The larger number is $x+16$.

$$\begin{align*}x^2+(x+16)^2&=130\\2x^2+32x+256&=130\\2x^2+32x+126&=0\\x^2+16x+63&=0\\(x+7)(x+9)&=0\end{align*}$$

By the null factor law, $x=-7$ or $x=-9$.

If $x=-7$, the larger number is $-7+16=9$.

If $x=-9$, the larger number is $-9+16=7$.

The numbers are $9$ and $-7$, or $7$ and $-9$. Both pairs have difference $16$ and squared sum $81+49=130$.

content.prompt: A triangle has base length 4 cm greater than its height. If the area of the triangle is $48\text{ cm}^2$, find the height of the triangle.

answer.worked:
Let $h$ cm be the height. The base is $(h+4)$ cm.

Using the triangle area formula:

$$\begin{align*}\frac12h(h+4)&=48\\h(h+4)&=96\\h^2+4h-96&=0\\(h+12)(h-8)&=0\\h&=-12\text{ or }h=8\end{align*}$$

The height must be positive, so the triangle has height $8\text{ cm}$.

A piece of sheet metal measuring $50\text{ cm}\times40\text{ cm}$ has squares cut out of each corner so that it can be bent and formed into an open box (with no lid) with a base area of $1344\text{ cm}^2$. Find the dimensions of the box.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Length}&=50-2(4)=42\text{ cm}\\\text{Width}&=40-2(4)=32\text{ cm}\\\text{Height}&=4\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

Hence the box measures $42\text{ cm}\times32\text{ cm}\times4\text{ cm}$. Its base area is $42\times32=1344\text{ cm}^2$.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ cm be the shorter side adjacent to the right angle. The other adjacent side is $(x+4)$ cm.

$$\begin{align*}\frac12x(x+4)&=48\\x(x+4)&=96\\x^2+4x-96&=0\\(x-8)(x+12)&=0\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}h^2&=8^2+12^2\\h^2&=208\\h&=\sqrt{208}\\h&=4\sqrt{13}\end{align*}$$

The three sides are $8\text{ cm}$, $12\text{ cm}$ and $4\sqrt{13}\text{ cm}$.

content.prompt: What must be added to each expression to make it a perfect square?

answer.worked:
Half the coefficient of $x$ is $2$, and $2^2=4$.
$$x^2+4x+4=(x+2)^2.$$

Half the coefficient of $x$ is $4$, and $4^2=16$.
$$x^2+8x+16=(x+4)^2.$$

Half the coefficient of $x$ is $-5$, and $(-5)^2=25$.
$$x^2-10x+25=(x-5)^2.$$

Half the coefficient of $x$ is $-6$, and $(-6)^2=36$.
$$x^2-12x+36=(x-6)^2.$$

Half the coefficient of $x$ is $10$, and $10^2=100$.
$$x^2+20x+100=(x+10)^2.$$

Half the coefficient of $x$ is $\frac{3}{2}$, and $\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^2=\frac{9}{4}$.
$$x^2+3x+\frac{9}{4}=\left(x+\frac{3}{2}\right)^2.$$

Half the coefficient of $x$ is $\frac{1}{2}$, and $\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2=\frac{1}{4}$.
$$x^2+x+\frac{1}{4}=\left(x+\frac{1}{2}\right)^2.$$

Half the coefficient of $x$ is $-\frac{7}{2}$, and $\left(-\frac{7}{2}\right)^2=\frac{49}{4}$.
$$x^2-7x+\frac{49}{4}=\left(x-\frac{7}{2}\right)^2.$$

Half the coefficient of $x$ is $-\frac{11}{2}$, and $\left(-\frac{11}{2}\right)^2=\frac{121}{4}$.
$$x^2-11x+\frac{121}{4}=\left(x-\frac{11}{2}\right)^2.$$

children.prompt: What positive real number is one more than its reciprocal?

answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the positive real number, so $x>0$.
$$\begin{align*}x&=1+\frac1x\\x^2&=x+1\\x^2-x-1&=0\end{align*}$$
Here $a=1$, $b=-1$, $c=-1$, so $b^2-4ac=1+4=5$.
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{1\pm\sqrt5}{2}\end{align*}$$
Reject $\dfrac{1-\sqrt5}{2}<0$. The required number is $\dfrac{1+\sqrt5}{2}$.
Check: its reciprocal is $\dfrac{\sqrt5-1}{2}$, and $1+\dfrac{\sqrt5-1}{2}=\dfrac{1+\sqrt5}{2}$.

children.prompt: A rectangle has length $5\text{ cm}$ greater than its width. If the area of the rectangle is $30\text{ cm}^2$, find the width of the rectangle (correct to two decimal places).

answer.worked:
Let the width be $x\text{ cm}$, where $x>0$. The length is $(x+5)\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}x(x+5)&=30\\x^2+5x-30&=0\end{align*}$$
Here $a=1$, $b=5$, $c=-30$, so $b^2-4ac=25+120=145$.
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{-5\pm\sqrt{145}}2\end{align*}$$
Reject the negative root. The width is $\dfrac{-5+\sqrt{145}}2\text{ cm}\approx3.52\text{ cm}$, correct to two decimal places.
Check using the exact dimensions:
$$\frac{\sqrt{145}-5}{2}\times\frac{\sqrt{145}+5}{2}=\frac{145-25}{4}=30.$$
Both dimensions are positive and differ by $5\text{ cm}$.

content.prompt: A farmer sells sheep at $\$75$ a head. The sheep cost $\$x$ each. The farmer finds he has made $x\%$ profit on the sale of the sheep. Find $x$.

x&=-150\quad\text{or}\quad x=50.

content.prompt: Find two numbers whose difference is 5 and the sum of whose squares is 100.

answer.short:
$\dfrac{5+5\sqrt7}{2}$ and $\dfrac{-5+5\sqrt7}{2}$, or $\dfrac{5-5\sqrt7}{2}$ and $\dfrac{-5-5\sqrt7}{2}$.

Represent the numbers as $x$ and $x-5$, then solve their sum-of-squares equation.
answer.worked:
Let the larger number be $x$, so the smaller number is $x-5$.
$$\begin{align*}x^2+(x-5)^2&=100\\x^2+x^2-10x+25&=100\\2x^2-10x-75&=0.\end{align*}$$
Here $a=2$, $b=-10$ and $c=-75$.
$$\begin{align*}b^2-4ac&=(-10)^2-4(2)(-75)\\b^2-4ac&=700.\end{align*}$$
Using the quadratic formula,
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{10\pm\sqrt{700}}{4}\\x&=\frac{5\pm5\sqrt7}{2}\\x-5&=\frac{-5\pm5\sqrt7}{2}.\end{align*}$$
The two pairs are therefore $\dfrac{5+5\sqrt7}{2}$ and $\dfrac{-5+5\sqrt7}{2}$, or $\dfrac{5-5\sqrt7}{2}$ and $\dfrac{-5-5\sqrt7}{2}$, taking matching signs.

Each pair has difference $5$. Writing either pair as $m+\frac52$ and $m-\frac52$, where $m=\pm\frac{5\sqrt7}{2}$, checks the sum of squares:
$$\begin{align*}\left(m+\frac52\right)^2+\left(m-\frac52\right)^2&=2m^2+\frac{25}{2}\\\left(m+\frac52\right)^2+\left(m-\frac52\right)^2&=2\left(\frac{175}{4}\right)+\frac{25}{2}\\\left(m+\frac52\right)^2+\left(m-\frac52\right)^2&=100.\end{align*}$$

content.prompt: An investor invests $\$10\,000$ at $x\%$ p.a. compound interest for 2 years. He finds that he receives $\$20$ more in interest than if he had invested it at a simple interest rate of $x\%$ p.a. Find $x$, correct to two decimal places.

answer.short: $x=2\sqrt5\approx4.47$, so the interest rate is $4.47\%$ p.a.
answer.worked:
With interest compounded annually, the compound interest and simple interest, in dollars, are
$$\begin{align*}I_C&=10\,000\left[\left(1+\frac{x}{100}\right)^2-1\right]\\I_C&=200x+x^2\\I_S&=10\,000\left(\frac{x}{100}\right)(2)\\I_S&=200x.\end{align*}$$
The compound interest exceeds the simple interest by $\$20$, so
$$\begin{align*}(200x+x^2)-200x&=20\\x^2&=20\\x&=\pm2\sqrt5.\end{align*}$$
The investment earns interest, so take the positive rate: $x=2\sqrt5\approx4.47$. Thus the rate is $4.47\%$ p.a., correct to two decimal places.

Check using the exact value: the extra interest is $(2\sqrt5)^2=20$ dollars.

content.prompt: A car travels 500 km at a constant speed. If it had travelled at a speed 10 km/h less, it would have taken 1 hour more to travel the distance. Find the speed of the car, correct to two decimal places.

answer.short:
$5(1+\sqrt{201})\text{ km/h}\approx75.89\text{ km/h}$.

Use time = distance ÷ speed to form a quadratic, then take the root greater than 10.
answer.worked:
Let the car's speed be $v$ km/h, where $v>10$. Using time = distance ÷ speed, the original time is $\frac{500}{v}$ hours and the slower journey takes $\frac{500}{v-10}$ hours.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{500}{v-10}&=\frac{500}{v}+1\\500v&=500(v-10)+v(v-10)\\500v&=500v-5000+v^2-10v\\v^2-10v-5000&=0.\end{align*}$$
Here $a=1$, $b=-10$ and $c=-5000$.
$$\begin{align*}b^2-4ac&=(-10)^2-4(1)(-5000)\\b^2-4ac&=20100.\end{align*}$$

children.prompt: The difference of two numbers is 16 and the sum of their squares is 130. What are the numbers?

answer.worked:
Let the smaller number be $x$, so the larger is $x+16$.
$$\begin{align*}x^2+(x+16)^2&=130\\2x^2+32x+256&=130\\2x^2+32x+126&=0\\x^2+16x+63&=0\\(x+7)(x+9)&=0\\x&=-7\quad\text{or}\quad x=-9\end{align*}$$
The numbers are $-7$ and $9$, or $-9$ and $7$. Each pair differs by $16$ and has sum of squares $49+81=130$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: The perimeter of a rectangle is 50 cm and its area is $144\text{ cm}^2$. Find its length and width.

answer.worked:
Let one side be $x\text{ cm}$. Since the perimeter is $50\text{ cm}$, the adjacent side is $(25-x)\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}x(25-x)&=144\\25x-x^2&=144\\x^2-25x+144&=0\\(x-9)(x-16)&=0\\x&=9\quad\text{or}\quad x=16\end{align*}$$
Both roots describe the same rectangle: length $16\text{ cm}$ and width $9\text{ cm}$. Its perimeter is $2(16+9)=50\text{ cm}$ and its area is $16\times9=144\text{ cm}^2$.

answer.short:

$$\begin{align*}(3x+1)^2+(5x-2)^2&=(5x)^2\\9x^2+6x+1+25x^2-20x+4&=25x^2\\9x^2-14x+5&=0\\9x^2-9x-5x+5&=0\\9x(x-1)-5(x-1)&=0\\(9x-5)(x-1)&=0\\9x-5&=0\quad\text{or}\quad x-1=0\\x&=\frac59\quad\text{or}\quad x=1\end{align*}$$

$x=0$ or $x=5a$, provided $a\ne0$. If $a=0$, there is no solution.

answer.worked:
The denominators require $x\ne-a$ and $x\ne\dfrac a2$. Multiplying by $(x+a)(2x-a)$ gives
$$\begin{align*}(x-a)(2x-a)&=(x+a)^2\\2x^2-3ax+a^2&=x^2+2ax+a^2\\x^2-5ax&=0\\x(x-5a)&=0.
\end{align*}$$
Thus $x=0$ or $x=5a$. For $a\ne0$, both satisfy the denominator restrictions and the original equation.

If $a=0$, the original equation requires $x\ne0$ and becomes $1=\tfrac12$, so there is no solution.

Quadratic equations turn up frequently in mathematics, and being able to solve them is a fundamental skill.

The ancient Babylonians were solving quadratic equations more than 5000 years ago!

Factorising general quadratic expressions
We will review a method of factorising general quadratic expressions when the coefficients do not have a common factor. There are a number of such methods, but we will only give one method here.
To factorise, for example, 3x² + 11x + 6, we go through the following steps.
First, we multiply the coefficient of x² by the constant term.
3 × 6 = 18
Next, we find two numbers with product 18 and sum 11, the coefficient of x. The numbers are 9 and 2. Using these numbers:
3x² + 11x + 6 = 3x² + 9x + 2x + 6 (Split the 11x term into 9x + 2x.)
= 3x(x + 3) + 2(x + 3) (Factorise in pairs.)
= (x + 3)(3x + 2) (Take out the common factor, (x + 3).)
It doesn’t matter if we split 11x as 2x + 9x instead.
Thus, 3x² + 11x + 6 = (x + 3)(3x + 2).
This is the method presented in Section 3G of this book.

entries.description:
Solution of quadratic equations by completing the square
• To solve a quadratic equation of the form ax² + bx + c = 0 by completing the square, we:
– move the constant, c, to the right-hand side
– divide all terms by the coefficient of x², a
– add the square of half the coefficient of x, (b/(2a))², to both sides of the equation
– solve for x.
• Fractions and square roots often occur in this procedure.
• We can also show that a quadratic equation has no solution using this procedure.

entries.description:
If b² − 4ac is negative, the equation has no solution. If b² − 4ac is positive or zero, then we can solve for x and obtain:
\(x+\frac{b}{2a}=\pm\sqrt{\frac{b^2-4ac}{4a^2}}\)
\(=\frac{\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}\quad\text{or}\quad-\frac{\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}\)
\(\therefore x=\frac{-b+\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}\quad\text{or}\quad\frac{-b-\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}\).

entries.description:

When solving ax² + bx + c = 0, first calculate b² − 4ac.

• If b² − 4ac = 0, then there is one solution: \(x=\frac{-b}{2a}\).

entries.description:
Solving quadratic equations – a summary
We now have three methods for solving a quadratic equation:
– completing the square
– factorisation
– the quadratic formula.
• It is a good idea to calculate b² − 4ac first to check that it is positive or zero, otherwise there will be no solution.
• Only use the quadratic formula or complete the square if you cannot see how to factorise the quadratic expression.
• When you use the quadratic formula, take care to simplify the surd and cancel any common factors.
• A quadratic equation for which the coefficient of x² is 1 and in which the coefficient of x is even can be solved more quickly and efficiently by completing the square than by using the quadratic formula. You should be in the habit of using both methods and, for a given situation, choosing the one you think will be the faster.

entries.description: The discriminant is the name given to b² − 4ac, the part of the quadratic formula under the square root sign. It is often denoted by the capital Greek letter delta, Δ (i.e. Δ = b² − 4ac). As noted, the discriminant can be used to determine the number of solutions in the quadratic equation. However, when a, b and c are rational numbers, and Δ > 0, it also determines the nature of the solution. If the discriminant is the square of a rational number (for example, 64, 1, 25, 1/4 or 49/36), then the solutions are rational numbers. Otherwise, the solutions contain a surd.
